text:
From H., I learned that I can be extremely close to someone and feel completely understood and supported without actually falling in love. I still treasure the support we gave/give each other.

Too many people judge a relationship only by whether they stayed together. Relationships are a process of growth in many dimensions, so start measuring what you actually learned from yours.
reader: someone reading an essay on romance for advice they can use in their own dating and relationships

sentences.s: From H., I learned that I can be extremely close to someone and feel completely understood and supported without actually falling in love.
sentences.payoff: they see that closeness and being understood can exist without falling in love.
sentences.follows: it opens the section on what was gained with a specific thing learned, though 'H.' needs earlier mention.

sentences.s: I still treasure the support we gave/give each other.
sentences.payoff: they see that the relationship still gave something lasting, the support.
sentences.follows: it extends S1 to what remains valued.

sentences.s: Too many people judge a relationship only by whether they stayed together.
sentences.payoff: they see that judging a relationship only by whether it lasted is common and a mistake.
sentences.follows: it turns from his case to the reader's, and the link to S2 is the staying together that did not happen.
sentences.link: none: turns from his case to the reader's

sentences.s: Relationships are a process of growth in many dimensions, so start measuring what you actually learned from yours.
sentences.payoff: they start measuring what they learned from their own relationships instead of whether they stayed.
sentences.follows: it gives the alternative to S3's measure.

placement: It depends on an earlier mention of H., and the heading 'loss' tells the reader the relationship ended; after that it runs lesson, value, mistake, alternative.

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
